items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You played with both of them... I’m wondering about your feelings about Blakey... Blakey would put you on fire... You played hard as a result of his approach and as a result of how he would accompany you

ctx.x: You played with both of them. I’m wondering about your feelings about Blakey, because that must have been early on. No, Blakey was the drummer on the thing from the air shots, too. [What were] your feelings about Blakey [and] about those two groups, because your writing crystallized that three-horn kind of writing– your feeling about the writing, about Blakey, [and] about those two sessions, if you remember.
First of all, it blows my mind to have someone make that kind of negative commentary about Art Blakey. [laughs] I don’t know who he was listening to. [Johnson continues laughing.]
They never heard of him again, I’m sure.
